summary_paragraph: A 30-year-old woman was readmitted on postpartum day 7 for severe-range hypertension and persistent headache, eight days after a spontaneous vaginal delivery complicated by preeclampsia and chorioamnionitis. She presented to gynecology triage with blood pressures in the 160–180s/80–100s and was treated with IV labetalol and started on oral nifedipine. Laboratory evaluation showed no signs of HELLP syndrome, and her symptoms improved with blood pressure control. She remained stable over 36 hours, with blood pressures maintained in the 120s/60s on nifedipine. Her headache resolved, and she was discharged home on antihypertensive therapy with plans to reschedule her outpatient electroconvulsive therapy. Follow-up was arranged with obstetrics and primary care.
problems: Other viral diseases complicating the puerperium
